title: The rescue ledger
bodyMd:
A fictional food-rescue group recorded kilograms of surplus produce collected from shops. Its weekly total rose sharply after a new supermarket joined. Volunteers celebrated until they noticed that much of the additional produce spoiled before distribution. Storage and transport, rather than available donations, had become the bottleneck.

The group began recording edible food actually delivered as well as food collected. It also asked some donors to provide smaller, more predictable quantities. This lowered the collection total but improved the amount reaching households. A sponsor initially worried that the smaller headline number signalled retreat. The coordinator replied that an activity measure had been mistaken for an outcome measure. Collecting more was useful only when the organisation could turn those collections into food that people could use.
